Ăchĕrūsĭus (old writing Acherunsius), a, um, adj. id..
I. Pertaining to the Acheron in Calabria: “aqua,” Liv. 8, 24 .—
II. Pertaining to the Acheruns (Acheron), or the Lower World: templa, the Lower World, Enn. ap. Cic. Tusc. 1, 21, 48 (Trag. v. 107 ed. Vahl.); in Varr. L. L. 7, § 6 Müll.; and in Lucr. 1, 120; cf. Lucr. 3, 25 and 86: “humor,” Sil. 13, 398 : “vita,” a life of gloom, Lucr. 3, 1024 .—
III. Pertaining to Acheron in Epirus: “amnis,” Just. 12, 2, 3 .
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
